artifacts.title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC conducted a full 42-hour trial of TE Daniel Herron of Central Indiana Presbytery on charges arising from allegations of sexual harassment and bullying, referred to the SJC by CIP under BCO 41. The SJC acquitted TE Herron on all charges, removed all censures and administrative suspensions imposed by CIP, and restored him to good standing as a PCA minister.

artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace PCA in Ohio excommunicated Travis and Sherylyn Dougherty for heresy (Trinitarian partialism) without separately establishing contumacy. Ohio Presbytery reversed the excommunication but failed to impose any new censure or remand the matter to Session; the SJC sustained the complaint in part, finding Presbytery correctly overturned the excommunication for lack of contumacy evidence but erred in leaving the guilty parties with no censure and in mandating the transfer of members to another church.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Charles Tarter appealed Evangel Presbytery's guilty verdict and censure after it convicted him of teaching a view of the creation days contrary to the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the appeal, vacated the judgment and censure, and remanded the matter because Presbytery had not followed the constitutional process for examining and recording a minister's stated differences; Presbytery was directed either to conduct that process or dismiss the case.

artifacts.title: Grady v. Southwest Florida
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission heard an appeal by TE John Grady from his conviction and censure by Southwest Florida Presbytery. The Commission sustained three of seven error specifications but found only one materially prejudicial. Critically, the Commission found that Presbytery misapplied BCO 13-9.c by claiming power to direct the minister to resign and then censuring him for refusal to comply; the Commission vacated the censure and remanded for reconsideration of appropriate punishment while the administrative suspension under BCO 31-10 remained in effect.

artifacts.title: Paul W. Lee v. Korean Southwest
artifacts.synopsis: Appeal by TE Paul W. Lee against Korean Southwest Presbytery's judgment finding him guilty of disobeying citations, rejecting admonitions, and other charges. The Standing Judicial Commission found KSWP erred on all issues through procedural violations including improper admonishment of judicial commission members mid-trial, failure to record trial proceedings, denial of cross-examination rights, and improper censure. Case remanded for retrial or dismissal.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Lachman appealed his conviction by the Session of Calvary Presbyterian Church on charges of violating the fifth, sixth, and ninth commandments through contentious correspondence and conduct, arguing the prosecution relied solely on documentary evidence without calling witnesses. The SJC denied the appeal, holding that documentary evidence combined with the appellant's acknowledgment of the letters constituted sufficient witness testimony; a concurring opinion recommended that Sessions facing strained relations with an accused elder consider referring such cases to Presbytery.

artifacts.title: Adams v. Northeast Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Philip J. Adams complained about a Northeast Presbytery judicial matter while a related appeal was pending and sought a retrial of charges on which the accused had been acquitted. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-1 and because the requested relief was unavailable. A separate opinion concurred in the result but dissented from part of the reasoning and urged clarification of appellate review after an acquittal.

artifacts.title: Elevating a censure without a new trial under BCO 36

matches.evidence: Proposed amendment to BCO 36 providing for censure elevation without a wholly new trial was found to be ambiguous under the BCO.

artifacts.title: Victim protection provisions in church discipline proceedings

matches.evidence: The CCB found that amending BCO 32-13 and 35-5 to allow victim protection measures in discipline proceedings was not in conflict with the BCO, and the overture was adopted.
